To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effect of menu labeling depends on the perceived healthfulness of the restaurant, and that consumers’ food choices are driven by different motivations at restaurants that are perceived as healthier or less healthy.
the effects of calorie information disclosure at restaurants on consumers’ food choice decisions depend on perceived healthfulness of the restaurant.
the effect of mandatory calorie information disclosure on food choices is moderated by the perceived healthfulness of the restaurant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the provision of calorie information influences consumers’ food choices.
the effect of calorie disclosure in the context of restaurant menus.
the effect of calorie disclosure on consumers’ restaurant food choices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calorie information disclosure is effective in helping consumers make healthier food choices at restaurants, but only when consumers perceive that restaurants are healthier.

calorie information disclosure is effective at restaurants that consumers perceive as healthy and that consumers perceive as unhealthy, but not at restaurants that consumers do not perceive as healthy or as unhealthy.
calorie information is effective at nudging consumers toward healthier choices, but only when consumers are exposed to the information in a context that is consistent with the information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calorie information disclosure has a significant effect on consumer behavior, but this effect depends on consumers’ perceptions of the restaurant.
calorie information disclosure has a significant impact on consumer’s food choice, but its impact is contingent upon perceived healthfulness of the restaurants.
calorie information disclosure can help consumers make healthier food choices, but the effect of calorie disclosure on consumers’ choices depends on the perceived healthfulness of the restaurants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mandatory calorie disclosure is unlikely to have the same effect at all restaurants.

calorie information disclosure is not a one-size-fits-all solution to encourage healthier food choices at restaurants, as the effect is contingent on consumers’ perceived healthfulness of the restaurant.
calorie information disclosure may be more effective at encouraging healthier food choices when used in conjunction with other interventions.
